fields.AN_Notes: Prompt experiment with ChatGPT (GPT-4) and Microsoft Copilot on four policy scenarios (restrooms, snow removal, office temperature, business-trip expenses), each prompt variant submitted 50 times in neutral, male, female and partly non-binary or new-mother versions; themes retained at a 70 percent threshold. Prompting is the research instrument and the object of the central finding. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: 'the importance of precise, inclusive language in AI-assisted design and policy applications', i.e. naming the gendered target group explicitly in the prompt; the work adds that equity principles must be embedded 'not just in prompts'. Other_Task: drafting workplace and municipal policy recommendations, outside social work. Bias_Axes: gender is varied in every scenario, and non-binary employees are an analysed group of their own (restroom and business-trip prompts), coded as Sexual_Orientation_Identity under the codebook label for gender identity; race, class and ability appear only as intersecting factors in the discussion, so Intersectional is not coded. Harm types from the work's own results: male default (Exclusionary_Norms), omission of women's and non-binary needs in unspecified prompts (Erasure), baby-changing facilities only in women's restrooms read as care stereotype (Stereotyping). Mitigation only proposed: curated gender-balanced and intersectional datasets (Pre_Processing), fine-tuning (In_Training), equity principles in prompts (Prompt_Practice), audits, Human-in-the-Loop oversight and multidisciplinary teams (Organisational_Process). Social_Construct rests on the applied statement after Connell that gender relations are institutionally embedded in everyday practices; the work also uses metabolic differences between women and men as a factual premise. Theory frame: Tronto's ethics of care, Young's justice as inclusion, capabilities approach, Connell, Grosz, feminist spatial planning, design justice.

fields.AN_Notes: Interpretative qualitative visual and intersectional analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from 18 deliberately minimal prompts (privilege and discrimination, ideology, everyday scenarios) on micro, meso and macro levels, complemented by a review of online and academic sources. Prompts serve as research instrument; minimal prompts simulate everyday internet users without prompt-engineering knowledge. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: users 'being more conscious of how they are generating images-e.g. what kind of prompts they use, and what kind of aesthetics they pick into the images'. AN_Task = None: the work audits default image outputs of the tool for everyday users and tests no professional application task; creative and design practice of artists appears as context and addressee of recommendations in the discussion. Axes from the own image analysis: gender, skin tone and ethnicity, disability, body size, age, wealth and class, immigrant/refugee versus citizen, Global North cultural hegemony, heteronormativity and absent non-binary representations; Intersectional from the micro-level analysis of the white, adult, able-bodied, heteronormative masculine default and single-axis diversification. Religion was excluded from the scope by the authors. Harm types: stereotyping, exclusion of feminine, non-binary and disabled representations (Erasure), white able-bodied masculine and Global North default (Exclusionary_Norms), reductionist portrayal of cultures and the Global South as poor (Misrepresentation). The confederate-flag finding concerns imagery, not language, so Toxicity is not coded. Mitigation only proposed within algorithmic reparation: curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), responsible designers, diverse teams, regulation and criminal culpability (Organisational_Process). Gender definition from footnote 2, which defines the binary gender norm and replaces man/woman by heteronormative feminine/masculine representations; it is a terminological determination rather than a definition of gender in the narrow sense.

fields.AN_Notes: Prompt tuning (trainable soft prompt embeddings concatenated to the input of frozen BERT and RoBERTa) as a debiasing method, trained on 159 gender-profession templates with a KL-divergence loss towards the average distribution across groups, evaluated on SEAT and StereoSet with language-modelling score and pseudo-perplexity against CDA, Dropout, INLP, SentenceDebias and Self-Debias. Generative_KI is teilweise: the work frames its object as large language models and language generation, but its method and experiments concern encoder-only masked language models. Prompting is the proposed mitigation practice; soft prompt tuning belongs to none of the technique families, and in-context learning appears only as motivation, so AN_Prompt_Techniques = None. Mitigation stage: the work places its intervention at inference ('additional information at inference') with model weights frozen, coded Intra_Processing; the trained parameters are prompt embeddings, not the model, so In_Training is not coded. The intervention changes the model input, coded Prompt_Practice. Evaluated with mixed results (on par with the state of the art, second to INLP on BERT). Axes: gender is the target; race and religion are measured as side effects on StereoSet. Harm type: stereotyping measured by the StereoSet stereotype score; the Gallegos harm list in the introduction is background and not coded. Gender is operationalised as he/she and male/female name pairs without a definition. Bias is determined technically by the stereotype score near 50 percent and by the reference distribution averaged across groups. AN_Task None: benchmark study without an application task.

fields.AN_Notes: Audit study with 42 prompt templates in five scenarios (purchase, chess, public office, sports, hiring) and 40 first names perceived as Black or white and male or female, 100 repetitions each, on GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Mistral Large and PaLM-2. Prompts are the research instrument, and the three context levels test prompt design. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: 'providing the model with a numeric anchor' (decision-relevant numeric information in the prompt), which the work's own experiment shows to remove name-based disparities in most scenarios, while qualitative context has inconsistent effects (Prompt_Practice, Evaluated); routine audits at deployment and implementation are recommended (Organisational_Process, Proposed). Other_Task: advice to laypeople in negotiation, hiring salary offers, election and sports predictions, outside social work. Intersectional is coded under the AN_Bias_Axes rule because Black female-perceived names yield the worst outcomes compared with Black and with female names, although the authors state that this analysis does not equate to an evaluation of intersectionality. Harm type: Indirect_Discrimination following the codebook anchor, since names act as proxies in numeric advice about persons (offers, salaries, chances) and the work interprets the disparities as disparate impact. The outputs are allocative decisions, not depictions of groups, and the encoded stereotypes are the authors' explanation of the mechanism; Stereotyping is therefore not coded as a separate representational harm. Gender is operationalised through male- and female-perceived names without definition. Bias is defined through the legal pair of disparate treatment and disparate impact, which also frames the interpretation (theory reference, a boundary case between legal doctrine and theory).
